page: Hetzner Cloud cx43 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 8 shared vCPUs with 8 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, provisioned via the QEMU hypervisor. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 160 GB NVMe SSD, while there are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. The processor supports AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average overall performance across most workloads. The stress-ng single-core CPU test shows strong performance in the top 25% at 2548.38, while multi-core performance sits in the average range at 20252.78. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 888.0 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 89.3 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server demonstrates weak performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 23.39 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 1233.0, but maintains average metrics in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the cx43 offers a budget-friendly resource profile for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves an average throughput of 10.98 GB/sec, as well as Redis key-value stores, processing 14.46 million SET operations per second. The server can handle light LLM inference tasks for small 135M models, but struggles with larger 7B models. It is best deployed for general-purpose utility tasks, development environments, and moderate web serving.
description: Hetzner Cloud cx43 is an x86_64 virtual server configured with 8 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 160 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on the QEMU hypervisor, it provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Performance benchmarks place the server mostly in the average tier, highlighted by strong single-core stress-ng performance but weaker single-threaded gzip compression and text processing. It achieves average results in software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. Lacking dedicated CPU cores and public IPv4 addresses, this server represents a cost-efficient option for budget-conscious deployments. It is best suited for development environments, static web hosting, Redis caching, and lightweight utility workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated compute resources.
